children: The shares of Biocon Ltd. saw modest gains on Friday, November 27 after the company announced that its biosimilar product had received regulatory approval in Brazil.

The company said its Hertuzo, a biosimilar of pertuzumab licensed to its partner Bionovis, received approval from Brazil's health regulator ANVISA to treat HER2-positive breast cancer across multiple stages of the disease, according to a regulatory filing on Friday.

Hertuzo is a biosimilar version of Perjeta, the reference biological medicine. ANVISA's approval was based on a comprehensive comparability assessment that demonstrated its similarity to the reference product.
Bionovis is a Brazilian biotechnology company focused on Research and Development and manufacturing of highly complex biologics.

“The approval of Hertuzo by Brazil’s ANVISA, following recent approvals of our biosimilar Pertuzumab in the United States and European Union, underscores Biocon’s scientific and regulatory capabilities and the growing strength of our global oncology portfolio,” said Susheel Umesh, Chief Commercial Officer for Emerging Markets and Head of Global API and Global Business Development at Biocon.
The approval followed Biocon securing a 10-year biosimilar pertuzumab Productive Development Partnership (PDP) in Brazil through a consortium with Bionovis and Bahiafarma, according to the filing.

Under the agreement, the consortium can supply locally manufactured biosimilar pertuzumab to Brazil's public healthcare market. This could expand access to the cancer treatment and reduce costs for the healthcare system, the filing said.

HER2-positive breast cancer is a subtype of breast cancer in which cancer cells produce excessive amounts of the HER2 protein, which promotes tumour growth. It accounts for around 15-20% of breast cancer cases and can be more aggressive than HER2-negative disease but responds to targeted treatments such as trastuzumab and pertuzumab.
Biocon's Recent US and European Approvals
The Brazilian approval adds to a series of regulatory clearances for Biocon's cancer treatment drugs this month.

On November 18, the company said the European Commission had granted marketing authorisation for Pebrilzo, its biosimilar pertuzumab, to treat HER2-positive breast cancer across multiple disease stages in the European Union.

Pebrilzo was the first pertuzumab biosimilar to receive European Commission marketing authorisation under the European Medicines Agency's (EMA) new tailored clinical approach, according to a regulatory filing back then.

On November 16, Biocon said the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) had approved Pebrilzo, a biosimilar to Perjeta. The company described it as its fifth USFDA-approved oncology biosimilar and said the approval would help expand affordable treatment options for patients with HER2-positive breast cancer.
Shares of Biocon are trading 0.3% higher on Friday at ₹366. The stock is still down 6% so far for the year.

title: Biocon shares gain after Brazil health regulator approves biosimilar for breast cancer drug
